intent: To illustrate the breakdown of Amazon's revenue by business segment (Online Store, AWS, Subscriptions, 3rd Party Retail) from 2015 to 2018, establishing the revenue composition before pivoting to a discussion on profitability.

requirements.question: Should the video be required to show Online Store as largest in every individual year, not just overall?
Is 3rd Party Retail's second-place ranking in each year required, or is Online Store dominance sufficient?
Should the video explicitly state that the two largest segments together dominate the composition, or is showing the individual segments enough?

units.claim: Online Store is the largest revenue segment in each year from 2015 to 2018, with relative values 0.65, 0.57, 0.60, and 0.65.
accept: Online Store is the biggest segment in every year, with relative values 0.65, 0.57, 0.60, 0.65.
The largest slice is always Online Store from 2015 through 2018.
Online Store dominates the revenue mix, about 0.6 relative value across the period.
units.evidence: In every year of the animation, the encoded mark for Online Store must be visually larger than the marks for 3rd Party Retail, AWS, and Subscriptions.

units.claim: 3rd Party Retail is the second-largest revenue segment in each year from 2015 to 2018, with relative values 0.20, 0.2998, 0.2501, and 0.20.
accept: 3rd Party Retail is always the second-biggest segment, with relative values 0.20, 0.2998, 0.2501, 0.20.
After Online Store, 3rd Party Retail is the next largest revenue source each year.
3rd Party Retail stays second in the revenue breakdown across 2015-2018.
units.evidence: In each year, the 3rd Party Retail mark must be visually larger than AWS and Subscriptions but smaller than Online Store.

units.claim: Online Store and 3rd Party Retail together make up the large majority of the relative revenue composition, about 0.85 to 0.87 in each year.
accept: Online Store plus 3rd Party Retail account for about 0.85-0.87 of the revenue mix each year.
The two largest segments together make up the vast majority of relative revenue.
Combined, Online Store and 3rd Party Retail stay around 0.85 relative value from 2015 to 2018.
units.evidence: In each year, the combined encoded area or attribute for Online Store and 3rd Party Retail must be visibly much larger than the combined AWS and Subscriptions portion.

optional_valid: 3rd Party Retail peaks in 2016 at relative value 0.2998, up from 0.20 in 2015 and back to 0.20 in 2018.
Online Store dips to 0.57 in 2016 before returning to 0.60 in 2017 and 0.65 in 2018.
AWS is about twice Subscriptions in 2015, 2017, and 2018 (0.10 vs 0.05, 0.0999 vs 0.0501, 0.10 vs 0.05), but not in 2016 (0.1002 vs 0.03).
Subscriptions has its lowest relative value in 2016 at 0.03.

g0_data_completeness.selection: all role=bar data rows; annotation rows excluded

hardcases.handling: Requires human visual inspection before semantic scoring.
